- Dependency plan: Doc 15 l53 and footnote 3 (title, January 2011, p.5; $500,000 "a low level") -> c3 and the paper's finding. Doc 5 l67-l75 ("Treasury's conclusion", footnote 13: same title and year) -> c2 and Treasury as author. Doc 8 l55 ("A consultation in 2011 asking this exact question identified that $500,000 was too low") matched to Doc 15's description by year, question and finding -> c1.
- Universe: every "2011", "options paper", "Future of Financial", "FOFA", "1991" and "consultation in" in the fifteen documents (searched 2026-10-14): D03 l30, l40 (1991), l55, l401 (a list row dated 1/11/2011); D04 l149 (FOFA reforms in 2012), l841 (2017 options paper on product rationalisation); D06 l75; D14 l53, l73, l167 (ASIC's 2011 submission to the Trio Capital inquiry, on business models, not thresholds). Also D01 l185 (Treasury's 2021 review of AFCA, not an options paper). Members: AIOFP, Angel Loop, Joint Associations.

Doc 5 is the only source of c2 and the only text naming Treasury as the paper's author; without it the answer is AIOFP, Joint Associations. Doc 15 is the only source of c3 and the only description of the paper's finding on $500,000, which identifies the AIOFP's consultation; without it the answer is Angel Loop (AIOFP by year alone at best). None is the gold; all three are answer components. Doc 2 (Allens) only introduces its own decoy and is not ticked; the reasoning names it without a Doc number, as on q01 and q02.

Scatter the pieces: the members sit in three documents, and the AIOFP member needs a second document to be identified.

All three screen solvers named this reading and rejected it. Considered and not declared: adding Allens (no screen solver took it); the Joint Associations split into its four bodies (the same set in another form).

- Semantic/ID/overview probes: no passage lists who relies on the paper. "Options paper" reaches D14 and D04; "Wholesale and Retail Clients" reaches D06 and D14; "2011" reaches D03 l55 (also D03 l401 and D14 l167). The screen solvers reached the AIOFP through "2011" and "consultation in" searches.

The AIOFP's year, question and finding all match and no other 2011 consultation on the threshold appears; reported as the reading most likely to be argued. (2) Doc 15's text says "Options Paper in 2010" while its footnote gives January 2011; same title; the footnote settles the date. (3) "Treasury's": only Doc 5 names the author ("Treasury's conclusion"). (4) Order: alphabetical by the names the submissions go by (AIOFP, Angel Loop, Joint Associations). Written out in full, Angel Loop sorts before the Association of Independently Owned Financial Professionals; two of the three screen solvers used that order. The set does not change. (5) "Rely on": each member uses the paper as support for its own position (raising the product value test; the s761GA pathway).
- Completeness: no source gaps; all fifteen documents read in full.

sections.question: Which submitters, if any, rely on Treasury's earlier options paper on wholesale and retail clients? List them alphabetically.
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 15, the Joint Associations' answer on the product value test, with its footnote 3): the Joint Associations cite the "Wholesale and Retail Clients Future of Financial Advice Options Paper, January 2011, p.5" for the finding that "the level of $500,000 was considered a low level", in support of raising the test. They rely on the paper (component c3).

Step 2. Source input (Doc 5, Angel Loop's answer on the thresholds, with its footnote 13): Angel Loop "agrees with Treasury's conclusion on the use of s761GA", quotes it, and cites "Wholesale and Retail Clients Future of Financial Advise 2011", the same paper by title and year. Angel Loop relies on the paper (component c2), and its words show the paper is Treasury's.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 8, the AIOFP's answer on the product value test, read with Doc 15): the AIOFP argues that the threshold should rise from $500,000 to $1,000,000 because "A consultation in 2011 asking this exact question identified that $500,000 was too low". It names no paper, but the year, the question and the finding all match the options paper as the Joint Associations describe it (January 2011; $500,000 "a low level"), and no submission mentions any other 2011 consultation on the threshold. The AIOFP relies on the same paper (component c1).

Decoy: Allens refers to a different Treasury options paper, on product rationalisation, and to the Future of Financial Advice reforms; neither is this paper, so Allens does not count.

Final answer, alphabetically by the names the submissions go by (Doc 8, Doc 5 and Doc 15): AIOFP, Angel Loop, Joint Associations (CA ANZ, CPA Australia, IPA, SMSF Association).
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Linking across documents: Doc 8 never names the paper; its "consultation in 2011" that found $500,000 too low matches Doc 15's January 2011 options paper. Counting only submitters that name it gives Angel Loop, Joint Associations; the gold adds AIOFP.
